Q: Do `setCustomValidity()` and `checkValidity()` supersede the need for external libraries? A:

For normal errors it's a nice function. For complex forms you may need external libraries or you have to write more code. For example you have a set of several check-boxes and user must check at least two of them. Another limitation of setCustomValidity is, the error message is just plain text and you cannot do any styling. If you like to provide fancy error message then setCustomValidity is not sufficient.

Q: Type Conversion Error in Copy activity for value 2150002867256: Azure data factory A:

Your data type of sink table schema column sourceKey must be INT(Transact-SQL):

The value '2150002867256' is out of the int range that caused the error. You could test is in SSMS and you will get the error:

You must change your sink table schema to other data type, for example bigint. It works well.

Q: How to disable statble sound in youtube iframe video player? A:

To disable unwanted sound or autoplay in a YouTube iframe video player, use these YouTube player settings in the video URL:

  • autoplay=0 → stops automatic playback

  • mute=1 → starts the video muted

  • controls=1 → keeps normal controls enabled

  • rel=0 → reduces unrelated suggested videos

Example URL format:

youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID?autoplay=0&mute=1&rel=0

If you mean a static/buzzing sound issue, then the problem is usually not the iframe itself. Common fixes are:

  • Try another browser

  • Disable browser extensions

  • Turn off hardware acceleration

  • Update audio drivers

  • Test with another YouTube video

  • Check headphones/speakers

YouTube itself does not provide a specific “disable stable/static sound” option inside the iframe player.

Q: Why does removing elements from a list inside a for loop skip items in Python? A:

There is 2 common methods to solve the skipping....

It frustrated me to when I was a beggnier..

So I wouldn't waste your time any more

Make a copy ([:]) of your list, here Loop runs on copy and elements removed from original

numbers = [1,2,2,3,4]

for num in numbers[:]: # Add copy here. 
    if num == 2:
        numbers.remove(num)

print(numbers) # output ==> [1,3,4]

This is on of the Most easiest way...

2nd Method :

Here we creat a new list in order to eliminate skip problem. so instead of using remove() we creat a new = [] list. and inside for we don't add numbers.remove(num). Instead we use new.append(num)..

numbers = [1,2,2,3,4] 

new = [] # add new list. 

for num in numbers:
    if num != 2: # notice operator.
        new.append(num) # use of append. 


print(new) # output ==> [1,3,4]

What actually we did here?.

we created new list old list is same no chnages...

We use new.append(num) to make chnages in new list old list is still same, all these changes happened in new list. That's how people's test list without effecting their old list..

But still output will be [1,3,4] cuz we printed new list.

So the structure should be look like this

Old list → check → keep good items → new list

Q: Why is sidebase/nuxt-auth not working in production without ssr? A:

this usually happens because @sidebase/nuxt-auth is not really designed to run as a pure SPA (ssr: false) app.

it relies heavily on the server layer Nuxt provides (server routes + session handling). things like getServerSession() and the built-in auth endpoints expect a working SSR/server runtime.

when you disable SSR, Nuxt basically becomes a client-only app, so those server-based pieces either don’t run or behave differently. in dev it can sometimes look fine because Nuxt still has a dev server running, but in production SPA mode the auth flow breaks.

so the main issue is not a bug in nuxt-auth, but a mismatch between the auth strategy and the rendering mode.

if you really need ssr: false, you’ll probably need to switch to a client-side auth approach (like JWT stored in cookies/localStorage + your own API handling) instead of relying on nuxt-auth’s server session system.
